ai.description: This 20–25 mm frog is yellow-green with dark brown mottling. It features a prominent, translucent yellow vocal sac and distinct, large, dark-pigmented eyes. It belongs to the family Rhacophoridae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes nerostagona* is best distinguished by the prominent, bright yellow, glandular spots scattered across its dark brown or reddish-brown dorsal skin.
ai.habitat: The Kalpatta Yellow Bush Frog inhabits the mid-to-high elevation evergreen forests and tea plantations of the Western Ghats, typically found at altitudes above 800 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kalpatta Yellow Bush Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining hidden within dense vegetation during the day and emerging at night to forage for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes nerostagona* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. It breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in arboreal foam nests.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes nerostagona* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, typically found at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Kalpatta Yellow Bush Frog emits a high-pitched, rhythmic "tink-tink" call, typically heard from vegetation near forest streams during the monsoon.
